assessmentSummary.identity: Dead Bug Heel Tap is an arms-vertical, supine tabletop, legs-only alternating heel-contact-and-return cycle. One side lowers through a comfortable active range to a light declared heel target, returns to the same tabletop, then the other side repeats. It is not an opposite arm-and-leg reach, heel slide, static press, wall press, loaded pullover, band task, Bird Dog, test, or forced range.
currentCardFindings: Source 66 was consolidated with a duplicate source but has not yet received an exact candidate-materialization contract.
The Dead Bug family audit already establishes arms-fixed legs-only heel contact as distinct from the generic contralateral Dead Bug.

proposedTaxonomy.laterality: alternating legs; arms remain fixed vertically

assessmentSummary.programmingDecision: Materialize Source 66 as a candidate-only arms-fixed alternating heel-tap definition; retain the consolidated progression source as lineage, use target/range/tempo as modifiers, and keep arm motion, continuous floor slide, isometric force, external resistance, and quadruped work separate.

currentCardSnapshot.description: Lie supine with hips and knees in tabletop and arms vertical. Keeping the arms fixed, lower one bent leg through a comfortable active range to a light declared heel target, return to the same tabletop, then alternate sides. One cycle is one controlled heel contact and return per side. This excludes contralateral arm-and-leg Dead Bug, heel slide, static press, wall press, pullover, band resistance, Bird Dog, testing, and forced range.

environment.space: room to lie, move each leg, and exit safely
environment.changeRule: Changing arm action, leg path, terminal contact, range, tempo, force, surface, dose, or intent requires revalidation.

selectionPrerequisites: can use the supine tabletop base and exit safely
can complete a small arms-fixed heel-contact return without symptom escalation or persistent trunk loss
session logistics and downstream demands fit
excludeOrEscalate: symptom, restriction, unsafe base, surface, or communication conflict
sharp, increasing, unfamiliar, neurologic, circulation, breathing, chest, balance, or communication concern
notEstablishedByEvidence: universal heel target, limb range, tabletop position, dose, recovery, outcome, readiness threshold, or clinical clearance

claims: Dead Bug Heel Tap is a supine tabletop, arms-vertical, legs-only alternating heel-contact-and-return cycle.
It excludes contralateral arm-and-leg Dead Bug, heel slide, static press, wall press, pullover, band resistance, crawling, testing, and forced range.
Arms remain fixed vertically while one bent leg lowers to a declared light heel target, returns to tabletop, and the other side repeats.
Range, cadence, and a brief pause are modifiers only while the arms-fixed alternating heel-contact return cycle remains intact.

claims: Record abdominal-wall, hip-flexor, shoulder-support, spine, pelvis, hip, and knee roles as task mechanics only; do not claim diagnosis or isolated activation.

evidence.sourceTitle: Changes in muscle activity of the abdominal muscles according to exercise method and speed during dead bug exercise
claims: Leg action and speed change measured activity; use a controlled heel touch and return rather than a dropped leg or lumbar-driven range.

evidence.sourceTitle: Youth Resistance Training: Updated Position Statement Paper From the NSCA
claims: Difficulty describes task complexity and physical demand only, never participant skill, age, proficiency, or classification.

evidence.sourceTitle: Changes in muscle activity of the abdominal muscles according to exercise method and speed during dead bug exercise
claims: Track side repetitions, heel target, range, tempo, rib/pelvis compensation, breath, neck tension, symptoms, and downstream trunk work; no universal recovery is claimed.

evidence.sourceTitle: Youth Resistance Training: Updated Position Statement Paper From the NSCA
claims: A clear stable floor or mat, space to lie and exit, optional padding, and communication are practical safeguards.
No universal dose or limb range is established; use a low-dose quality-limited candidate prescription and stop before persistent compensation or symptoms.
Instructions must name tabletop, arms vertical, one heel lowering, light target contact, controlled return, alternation, breathing, and reset.

evidence.sourceTitle: Youth Resistance Training: Updated Position Statement Paper From the NSCA
claims: Stop for pain, new neurologic/circulation/breathing/dizziness symptoms, pressure concern, unsafe surface, persistent breath holding, or uncorrectable quality loss.

evidence.sourceTitle: Changes in muscle activity of the abdominal muscles according to exercise method and speed during dead bug exercise
claims: Use the exact low-load arms-fixed heel-tap task only when it fits the session; altered limbs, force, range, dose, or substitution rerun validation.
Athlete support should show the tabletop start, light heel target, quiet trunk, return, side change, self-check, and stop prompt.

evidence.sourceTitle: Changes in muscle activity of the abdominal muscles according to exercise method and speed during dead bug exercise
claims: Observe arm fixation, heel target, range, trunk/pelvis, breathing, return, side count, and first quality loss; do not diagnose a stability deficit.

evidence.sourceTitle: Youth Resistance Training: Updated Position Statement Paper From the NSCA
claims: Padding, a smaller range, fewer repetitions, longer rest, still sequence, captions, transcript, audio description, and a reviewed substitute are candidate supports, not readiness proof.

Brief pause, target height, range, and tempo can be modifiers. Heel slides, arm-and-leg reaches, static presses, wall presses, pullover/band loading, and Bird Dog change the task contract and require separate assessment.
Three inherited direct YouTube URLs are retained only as unverified candidates; no playback, exact-match, accessibility, quality, reviewer, or approval claim is made.

alternateAssessments.name: Dead Bug Heel Tap with Brief Pause
alternateAssessments.rationale: A declared short pause preserves the arms-fixed alternating heel-contact return cycle.

alternateAssessments.rationale: A declared shorter range preserves the exact limb action and return.

alternateAssessments.name: Dead Bug Heel Slide
alternateAssessments.rationale: Continuous floor contact changes the leg path and terminal condition.

alternateAssessments.name: Contralateral Arm and Heel-Tap Dead Bug
alternateAssessments.rationale: Adding opposite-arm motion changes coordination and support demand.

alternateAssessments.name: Dead Bug Iso Press
alternateAssessments.rationale: Isometric hand-to-knee or ball force changes primary action and dose.

alternateAssessments.name: Dead Bug Wall Press
alternateAssessments.rationale: A fixed bilateral wall press changes hand constraint and equipment.

alternateAssessments.name: Bird Dog
alternateAssessments.rationale: A quadruped base changes support geometry and task action.
